-87.63890,41.86750.name: University of Chicago Medicine Center for Reproductive Medicine and Fertility
-87.63890,41.86750.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: A. Musa Zamah, MD, PHD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-0.20763,50.83192.name: Sussex Sperm Bank
-0.20763,50.83192.state: 16-17, Boundary Road, East Sussex, Hove, BN3 4EF
-0.20763,50.83192.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-125.13486,48.83454.name: Bamfield Marine Sciences Centre
-125.13486,48.83454.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, July 2025
-125.13486,48.83454.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, July 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-71.08500,42.36600.name: Bluebird bio
-71.08500,42.36600.desc: Approved gene therapies for beta-thalassemia and cerebral adrenoleukodystrophy, then withdrew from Europe entirely when governments would not meet its price, and later reported a quarter with no doses sold at all in the United States. Patients who could have had a working treatment simply cannot get one. It is the clearest demonstration that a cure existing and a cure being available are different facts.

-71.08500,42.36600.name: bluebird bio — the insertional oncogenesis cases
-71.08500,42.36600.desc: Patients treated with the company’s gene therapy later developed blood cancers, and trials were paused while whether the vector caused them was investigated. A therapy that inserts DNA into a patient’s genome can land somewhere that matters, and these are the documented cases.

-71.08500,42.36600.name: Generate Biomedicines
-71.08500,42.36600.desc: Uses generative models to design therapeutic proteins from scratch rather than screening existing ones. When a molecule is designed rather than found, the regulatory question of what it is derived from has no answer, because it is not derived from anything.

38.74690,9.03200.name: Ethiopian Environment Protection Authority — biosafety
38.74690,9.03200.desc: Ethiopia rewrote a restrictive biosafety law to permit engineered cotton and maize trials. Law reform preceding approval is the standard sequence across Africa, and the pressure for it typically comes from a combination of donor programmes and neighbouring states’ decisions.

38.74690,9.03200.name: African Union — continental biosafety and biotechnology policy
38.74690,9.03200.desc: Continental coordination on biosafety policy through AUDA-NEPAD, providing model law and technical support to member states. Where a country has no capacity to assess an application, the assessment is effectively imported — and the continent's regulatory direction is therefore set in a small number of places rather than in fifty-five separate debates.

-71.12100,42.39600.name: Greenlight Biosciences
-71.12100,42.39600.desc: Produces sprayed double-stranded RNA that silences a gene in a target pest, with no organism modified. No biosafety framework applies because nothing living is altered, and pesticide assumptions about dose and residue do not fit a sequence-specific mechanism. Both categories were built for something else, and the product sells while the question of which governs it stays open.

-121.74000,38.54500.name: Arcadia Biosciences
-121.74000,38.54500.desc: Developed wheat and other crops with altered nutritional composition, including reduced-gluten wheat, using both conventional and engineered approaches. It is a long-running example of the output trait — a change a consumer might want rather than one a farmer wants — which has repeatedly been promised as the next phase of this industry and repeatedly not arrived.

6.15000,62.47000.name: Farmed salmon genetics established in wild Norwegian rivers
6.15000,62.47000.type: Salmon, genetic introgression into wild populations
6.15000,62.47000.status: Documented in a majority of assessed rivers
6.15000,62.47000.desc: Norwegian monitoring finds farmed salmon genetics in a large majority of assessed wild rivers. Nothing engineered is involved: intensive selection plus escapes from pens has already changed wild fish, which is the baseline any argument about engineered salmon starts from.

116.29600,40.04800.name: EdiGene
116.29600,40.04800.desc: Runs gene-editing therapy programmes in China, including for blood disorders, under a domestic approval route rather than the FDA or EMA. China has authorised cell and gene therapies its Western counterparts have not, and this is one of the companies working through that difference.

6.13300,49.61200.name: Confédération paysanne — editing is genetic modification
6.13300,49.61200.state: Luxembourg — Court of Justice of the European Union
6.13300,49.61200.desc: The European Court of Justice held in 2018 that organisms produced by newer mutagenesis techniques are genetically modified organisms within the directive, and are not covered by the exemption for conventional mutagenesis. It is why edited crops are regulated in the EU and unregulated in most of the Americas, and why the Commission has since proposed legislation to reverse it. Every argument about whether editing counts refers back to this.

5.50000,51.70000.name: Stichting Taurus
5.50000,51.70000.state: Netherlands — with breeding herds in six countries
5.50000,51.70000.desc: The Dutch foundation that started the Tauros Programme in 2008 and runs its breeding, with scientific support from Wageningen University. The aurochs was hunted to extinction in 1627 but its genetics survive dispersed among older cattle breeds, and the programme crosses the closest of those breeds toward an animal that can graze European landscapes without supplementary feeding and alongside predators. A 2016 genetic study ranked 34 primitive breeds by closeness to a 6,700-year-old sequenced aurochs genome, which is how the parent stock is chosen. This is the entry that puts the rest of the facet in proportion: it pursues the same goal as the venture-funded de-extinction companies — an extinct animal's ecological function restored — using crossbreeding, published genomics and two decades, with no editing, no cloning, and no surrogate mothers.
